Project file 03 / architecture ongoing

PULSAR-4X —
four clocks, one stream.

Four-channel, 8-bit time-interleaved SAR ADC architecture for a high-speed SerDes receiver.

TSMC 65 nm GP · architecture targetNot taped out
01 / System goal
02 / Architecture
03 / Targets
04 / Risks

The system goal

Explore a four-channel time-interleaved converter for a PAM4 SerDes receive front end. The system must balance conversion throughput against inter-channel timing mismatch, offset and gain error.

Architecture direction

Each channel uses an 8-bit nonbinary SAR conversion with loop-unrolled 2-bit-per-cycle decisions. Four channels are time-interleaved and followed by a 4:1 mux/deskew path. Background calibration is planned for offset, gain, sampling skew and comparator mismatch.

Target only: 4 channels × 500 MS/s each = 2.0 GS/s aggregate. These are architectural targets; no silicon measurements exist.

Other stated targets

  • 5–6 conversion cycles per channel.
  • Less than 1.0 ps RMS inter-channel sampling skew.
  • 33.4 mW typical and 41.2 mW maximum total power targets.

Open work

Prove the nonbinary search margins, quantify calibration convergence and stability, and close the circuit-level power and noise budget before treating any of these numbers as achievable implementation results.
